intent: A drowned fishing coast of wet slate-grey shingle, black rock and bleached driftwood, with pale sea-green tide-pools and kelp, a dead lighthouse and a great wreck for landmarks, reading from the high camera as a cold grey shore broken by cold sea-green phosphorescence.
requests: A wreck kind: a beached hull's curved ribs, since the bones kind always grows a horned skull and so the great wreck reads partly as a sea-beast.
A water or flood ground material, or a way to lay tide-pools over open heath: pools only appear where the terrace rules hollow the ground, so the half-tide-pool ground can't be painted.
